guide.summary: Restricted Mode, up to 25 outside users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Public app, Restricted Mode removed (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Restricted Mode, up to 25 outside users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Public app, Restricted Mode removed (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).

composio.note: Composio has managed OAuth for YNAB, which is fine for prototypes. For production, create an auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: For a prototype, no: Composio's managed app works. For production you want your own app, so users see your name, you get your own quota, and you can control scopes and review status.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Custom scopes require your own app
Your own app is the one YNAB reviews and lifts from Restricted Mode

scenarios.when_this_applies: Production agent serving more than 25 outside YNAB users.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

prerequisites.title: YNAB account with Developer Settings
prerequisites.detail: Sign in to YNAB, open Account Settings, then Developer Settings, and add a New Application under OAuth Applications.

prerequisites.title: Published privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: It must show a Last Updated date and a way for users to delete their data (a contact email works). Show its URL in the OAuth client configuration and in your app.

prerequisites.title: Compliant app name and disclaimer
prerequisites.detail: Use 'for YNAB' naming if the name or domain includes YNAB, and put a non-affiliation disclaimer in the site footer.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Get the Composio redirect URI for the YNAB toolkit from the dashboard.

steps.title: Create the YNAB OAuth application
steps.detail: In Developer Settings click New Application, enter details and the redirect URI, then save. The client ID and secret are then shown.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are visible.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Use Composio's API to create a custom OAuth2 auth config for the ynab toolkit with your client ID and secret. Request read-only scope if you do not need writes.

steps.title: Draft privacy policy and disclaimer text
steps.detail: Draft the policy with a Last Updated date and a deletion method. Also draft the footer disclaimer and check the app name against the 'for YNAB' rule.

steps.title: Publish policy and disclaimer
steps.detail: Review the drafts, publish them, and add the privacy policy URL to the OAuth app configuration.
steps.done_when: Pages are live and URL is set in the app.

steps.title: Test connections with a non-owner user
steps.detail: Run a connect flow and a read call, and check token refresh handling.
steps.done_when: A non-owner account connects and reads data.

steps.title: Submit Restricted Mode removal request
steps.detail: Fill in the review form from the YNAB API docs and submit it before you pass 25 users.

steps.title: Wait for YNAB review
steps.detail: YNAB reviews policy adherence and emails you when Restricted Mode is removed.

traps.title: An access token may be used for up to
traps.detail: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour, enforced in a rolling one-hour window.

traps.title: The 25-token cap blocks new users
traps.detail: After 25 outside users, the authorization screen shows a message and blocks new authorizations. Beeminder launched on restricted access and admitted it should have applied for full access first.

traps.title: Apply for review before launch
traps.detail: The review takes 2-4 weeks, and one user report suggests a first reply could take up to a week.

traps.title: Personal access tokens are not for customers
traps.detail: OAuth is the only option for tokens for other users. Personal tokens are for the account owner only.

traps.title: Tokens expire after 2 hours
traps.detail: Implicit grant has no refresh tokens, so users must re-authorize. Authorization code grant supports refresh tokens.

traps.title: Rate limit is 200 requests per hour per token
Policy violations disable the app
traps.detail: Non-compliance with the API Terms or OAuth requirements disables the app. Never handle users' financial account credentials, and do not sell YNAB user data.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding and shares quota
traps.detail: Fine for prototypes, but users see 'Composio wants to access your account', and quota is shared across Composio users.

blockers.symptom: Authorization screen shows a limit message and new users cannot authorize
blockers.what_it_means: The app is in Restricted Mode and has reached 25 non-owner tokens.
blockers.what_to_do: Request Restricted Mode removal through YNAB's review form and wait 2-4 weeks.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare the privacy policy and app details for the form.

blockers.symptom: 403 Forbidden on POST or PATCH requests
blockers.what_it_means: The token was issued with the read-only scope.
blockers.what_to_do: Request a broader scope only if writes are needed; otherwise keep read-only.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check which scope the auth config requests.

blockers.what_it_means: The user's YNAB subscription has lapsed.
blockers.what_to_do: Tell the user to renew their subscription.
blockers.agent_can_help: Detect the error and show a clear message.

open_questions: Do any YNAB-specific rules apply to AI agents? Check the OAuth Application Requirements and API Terms, or ask YNAB support.
How long does YNAB take to reply once a review request is submitted? Only the documented 2-4 weeks and one anecdotal report exist; ask YNAB support.
Does a customer's workspace admin need to approve connections? Not found; test with a real team account.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: | [YNAB](/toolkits/ynab.md) | `YNAB` |
evidence.answer: YNAB is listed under the Composio-managed OAuth available group, so Composio provides the OAuth app for it.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit. You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: Composio can provide the OAuth app that users authorize when they connect a toolkit, so the developer does not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If `composio_managed_auth_schemes` contains the toolkit's OAuth method, Composio provides the OAuth app. If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: Whether Composio provides the OAuth app is determined by checking whether the toolkit's OAuth method appears in composio_managed_auth_schemes from the toolkit endpoint; if not, you must register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and secret.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method. A toolkit appears under **Composio-managed OAuth available** when Composio manages at least one OAuth method. Open the toolkit page to check each method.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method, and a toolkit is listed as Composio-managed when Composio manages at least one OAuth method, so each method must be checked on the toolkit's page.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Scope: use the minimum viable scope. Prefer read-only unless the hosted connector explicitly offers write tools.
evidence.answer: For this YNAB connector, the scope should be the minimum viable one, and read-only is preferred unless the connector explicitly offers write tools.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Register write tools only when the connector grant, deployment config, and requested YNAB scope all allow writes.
evidence.answer: For this YNAB connector, write tools are registered only when the connector grant, deployment config, and requested YNAB scope all allow writes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Remember the client-enablement caveat: some clients require a developer/beta mode or workspace-admin approval before they expose or invoke custom-connector write tools, independent of the YNAB grant.
evidence.answer: Some MCP clients need developer/beta mode or workspace-admin approval before they expose or invoke custom-connector write tools, separately from the YNAB grant.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: The connector's public origin is used to build the exact callback URI for the YNAB OAuth flow.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: The hosted YNAB connector exposes MCP over HTTPS.

evidence.answer: The developer must create and verify a YNAB OAuth application that uses the production redirect URI.

evidence.answer: The YNAB OAuth authorization URL is https://app.ynab.com/oauth/authorize.

evidence.answer: The privacy policy must give a method for users to delete their data if requested.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Display the privacy policy URL in your OAuth client configuration when your application is publicly available and ensure that it is prominently displayed in your application interface so that users can find this information easily.
evidence.answer: The privacy policy URL must be displayed in the OAuth client configuration when the app is publicly available.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: When an OAuth application is requesting authorization, a scope parameter with a value of read-only can be passed to request read-only access to a plan.
evidence.answer: A read-only scope can be requested so the app gets read-only access to a plan.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If an access token issued with the read-only scope is used when requesting an endpoint that modifies the plan (POST, PATCH, etc.) a 403 Forbidden response will be issued.
evidence.answer: A token with the read-only scope gets a 403 Forbidden response on requests that modify the plan (POST, PATCH, etc.).

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If you do not need write access to a plan, please use the read-only scope.
evidence.answer: Developers are told to use the read-only scope when they do not need write access, and to request only the minimum permissions needed.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Only request the minimum necessary permissions to run your application, features, or services and don’t request access to information that you don’t need.
evidence.answer: Developers should request only the minimum necessary permissions and request access in context via incremental authorization where possible.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This means the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner.
evidence.answer: Unreviewed (Restricted Mode) OAuth apps are limited to 25 access tokens for users other than the owner.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour
evidence.answer: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour, enforced in a rolling one-hour window.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type does not support refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the user must be prompted again to authorize your application.
evidence.answer: Implicit Grant access tokens expire 2 hours after being granted, and there are no refresh tokens, so the user must re-authorize.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type supports refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the application can request a new access token without having to prompt the user to authorize again.
evidence.answer: Authorization Code Grant access tokens expire 2 hours after being granted, but refresh tokens allow renewal without re-prompting the user.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: Restricted Mode removal review takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The subscription for this account has lapsed
evidence.answer: A 403.1 subscription_lapsed error is returned when the subscription for the account has lapsed.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The trial for this account has expired
evidence.answer: A 403.2 trial_expired error is returned when the trial for the account has expired.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: build an application that any other YNABer can authorize and use.
evidence.answer: Any other YNAB user can authorize and use an app built on the API.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may only be used when permission is explicitly given by a YNAB account owner through the Authentication processes described in the documentation above.
evidence.answer: The API may only be used when a YNAB account owner explicitly gives permission through the documented authentication processes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The user will be given the option to approve your request for access:
evidence.answer: The authorizing user is shown an option to approve the app's access request.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When default plan selection is enabled, a user will be asked to select a default plan when authorizing your application:
evidence.answer: If default plan selection is enabled, the user is asked to pick a default plan when authorizing the app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: replacing [CLIENT_ID] and [REDIRECT_URI] with the values configured when creating the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The client ID and redirect URI used in the authorization URL must be the values configured when the OAuth app was created.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The same [REDIRECT_URI] sent with the original authorization code request in Step 1 above and specified when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The redirect_uri in the token request must match the one sent in the authorization request and specified when setting up the app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Upon user approval, the server will send an Authorization Response and the user's browser will be redirected to the [REDIRECT_URI] with a new access token sent as a fragment (hash) identifier named access_token .
evidence.answer: In the Implicit Grant, the browser is redirected to the redirect URI with the access token in the URL fragment.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: TLS (a.k.a. SSL or HTTPS) is enforced on all requests to ensure communication from your client to our endpoint is encrypted,
evidence.answer: TLS (HTTPS) is enforced on all API requests, so communication to the endpoint is encrypted.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After saving, you will see the details of the new application, including the Client ID and the Client Secret which are referenced in the instructions below.
evidence.answer: After saving a new OAuth application, its Client ID and Client Secret are shown on the app details page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Here, you specify the details of your application and save it.
evidence.answer: When creating the app, you specify its details and save it, which is when the redirect URI is set.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: An OAuth application can optionally have 'default plan selection' enabled.
evidence.answer: Default plan selection is an optional setting that can be enabled for an OAuth application.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application and the web address (DNS name) must not include "YNAB" or "You Need A Budget" unless preceded by the word "for".
evidence.answer: Apps must not use the name 'YNAB' or 'You Need A Budget' (or the DNS name) unless preceded by the word 'for'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You and your integration or app may not identify or refer to YNAB in any manner that creates a false suggestion (either directly or indirectly!) that an application is sponsored, endorsed, or supported by YNAB.
evidence.answer: Apps may not suggest, directly or indirectly, that YNAB sponsors, endorses or supports them.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.
evidence.answer: Apps may not use the API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You are NEVER ALLOWED to directly request, handle or store credentials associated with users’ financial accounts.
evidence.answer: Apps must not directly request, handle or store users' financial account credentials.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: access, aggregate, or analyze YNAB user data if the data will be sold to a third party
evidence.answer: Using YNAB user data for sale to a third party is prohibited.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application may not be directed or for children under 13. The minimum age for a user to use YNAB is 13.
evidence.answer: Applications may not be directed at children under 13, and the minimum age to use YNAB is 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: To use the YNAB API and accept the Terms you must be of a legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB.
evidence.answer: Users of the API must be of legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: We are not affiliated, associated, or in any way officially connected with YNAB or any of its subsidiaries or affiliates.
evidence.answer: Apps must show a disclaimer in the site footer that they are not affiliated with YNAB.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: right now we’re using a restricted access to their API, which only has a limited number of “slots”. We should’ve applied for full access before launching the integration, but it slipped through the cracks.
evidence.answer: Beeminder's developer team (July 2024 forum report) launched a YNAB integration on restricted API access, which has a limited number of slots, and admitted they should have applied for full access before launch; this is a blocker to a launch-ready integration.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: based on the auto-reply we got from YNAB, it might take up to a week to get a response from them
evidence.answer: Per the same report, YNAB's auto-reply to the access request suggested up to a week before a response; this is a single anecdotal wait-time data point, not an official SLA.
